<!-- pr-reviewer: f8fc8be0c37afd3074665c65a8d8a4f6513bea07 -->
**Ready for the maintainer to merge** — green review on the PR head, against `origin/side/path-kernel` (171424230).

What looks good
- The mutation proof is real: each law file holds a stand-in that obeys the law and one or more that break it in a named way, and every breaking case is refused by the right check with the right message (verified by running the suite with --nocapture: L1 hidden state 0.255 vs limit 0.001, L1 loop-start seam 0.707, L1 shared guide 0.636, L3 moved 0.100 / dropped 1 curve (inf), L4 rows→rings 10 silent, L4 entry Ramp 1.0, L5 air proof 1.000, L6 slot read 0.987, L7 moved ring 0.127 / another direction 22.6, link uncounted lift 7, link on no-split fixture 9, link stay across island 7.0).
- The suite joins the existing directory suite `crates/pathkernel/tests/laws/` (law checks in-place, no new top-level test file, no xtask change) — as the issue asks.
- The decision file `docs/decisions/4027-kernel-law-suite.md` explains the suite, the stand-ins, the registry and the K1 interplay honestly, including the known limit that the entry stage has no fallback channel.
- `laws.rs` carries the provenance line for the suite; grid/kit/standins carry their own.

Results (trial merge with `origin/side/path-kernel` at `171424230`: clean, `Already up to date`)
- Linux, local worktree `cc-pr4175-review`, head `f8fc8be0c`.
- Quick gate `CAMCRAFT_GATE_JOBS=6 cargo xtask gate quick --base origin/side/path-kernel`: 1 step (`pathkernel suites: laws`), ok in 20s; 64 passed, 0 failed.
- `cargo test -p camcraft-pathkernel --test laws`: 64 passed, 0 failed (0.2 s).
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-pathkernel --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.
- Light lane `cargo xtask gate light`: 6 of 6 steps green (light build 686s, motion lib 338s, adaptive_troch_island 41s, adaptive_troch_neck 17s, adaptive_troch_parallel 11s, app pocket_pass_start 4s; wall 18.4 min)
- Example catalog suites: not run — no post or toolpath change.
- Targeted heavy step: not owed — this is a test-only PR (laws), not a safety-floor P1 change; no heavy step owed.

Requested before merge
1. (none blocking) — see notes.

Questions / notes
- The vacuous test `each_moved_kind_obeys_every_law` (all 16 rows are `NotYet`, so it loops over nothing) is intentional, but it only guards the table format; the real guard that a moved kind's recipe agrees with its row is `the_registry_guard_names_a_moved_kind_without_a_recipe` and `the_law_runner_passes_a_registered_kind_that_obeys_every_law`. Fine as designed; worth knowing.
- The registry path passes `&[]` for the L1 "other kinds with the same choice" check, so a future kind's guide is never compared against a real other kind's guide in the registry path (only via the synthetic other in `l1_guide.rs`). Worth wiring at the first moved kind.
- The L7 record for the registry is derived from the stand-in's own run (`stand_in_kind`), so the registered stand-in case is L7-trivial (the plan equals itself). The real record comes from the old planner's golden `.cl` at the move, as the decision doc says — fine, but worth stating.
- `check_l3` does not flag an all-refused run: if every start side refuses, the count pushed is `0` (`ok.is_empty()` → 0), so the law passes vacuously. The L7 check catches it when a non-empty old record exists, so it is not silent in the registry path, but the L3 check alone would wave it through. Consider making an all-refused case `named as refused / broken` next time the registry is touched.
- The PR body says "the 31 new tests in laws"; the actual count of new test fns across `l1_guide..registry` is 33 (l1:4, l2:3, l3:3, l4:3, l5:3, l6:2, l7:4, link_rule:4, registry:5). Cosmetic.
- No provenance comment on the individual law modules (`l1_guide` .. `l7_move`, `link_rule`, `registry`): the suite-level `laws.rs` carries the provenance and `grid.rs`/`kit.rs`/`standins.rs` carry their own, so this is a small consistency nit, not a violation of the Prime Directive.
- K1 (#4181) is in flight on the same side branch and changes the `PlanarRegion::new` signature and `construction.rs`/`laws.rs`. The PR body already records who fixes the two calls (`kit::rebuild`, `standins::pocket_region`) at merge time — and since construction.rs also calls `PlanarRegion::new` (line 97), the merge fix must also update that call. Worth a line in the PR body's merge-time fix note.

A maintainer will approve and merge by hand.
